inline_comments.comment:
Slot assignment bug when only a change icon exists and no test icon: the else branch of `{branchTestIcon ? ... }` renders `branchChangeIcon` in the second (test) slot while a `StatusSlotPlaceholder` occupies the first (change) slot. The result is the change-detection icon always landing in the wrong column.

Trace:
- Both present → slot 1: change ✓, slot 2: test ✓
- Change only → slot 1: `<StatusSlotPlaceholder />` ✗, slot 2: change icon ✗
- Test only → slot 1: placeholder, slot 2: test ✓

The simplest fix is to decouple the two slots so each renders independently:
```tsx
{branchChangeIcon ? (
  <StatusButton ariaLabel={`Change status: ...`} ...>{branchChangeIcon}</StatusButton>
) : branchTestIcon ? (
  <StatusSlotPlaceholder aria-hidden="true" />
) : null}
{branchTestIcon ? (
  <StatusButton ariaLabel={`Test status: ...`} ...>{branchTestIcon}</StatusButton>
) : null}
```
This ensures the change icon always occupies the first slot and the test icon always occupies the second.

`getChangeDetectionStatus(statuses || {})` is called here and internally computes both `changeStatus` and `testStatus`, but only `testStatus` is destructured and used — `changeStatus` is silently discarded for every leaf (story/docs) node. This means a story whose only status is `status-value:new` or `status-value:modified` renders no icon at all on the leaf row.

If the design intent is that change-detection is intentionally suppressed on leaf nodes (shown only on branch ancestors via `groupDualStatus`), then calling `getChangeDetectionStatus` here is wasteful: the non-change-detection values could be obtained with a direct filter without the overhead of computing the unused change slot. If leaf nodes should show both icons (as the PR description states: "two independent `StatusButton` components per leaf node"), then the change slot rendering is simply missing.

`getChangeDetectionStatus` is imported from `'../components/sidebar/Tree.tsx'` — a React component file — in a utility test. This is an unusual inversion: test infrastructure for status utilities shouldn't depend on a component module. The function has no React dependencies (no JSX, no hooks) and belongs in `status.tsx` alongside `getGroupDualStatus`. Moving it there would make this import `from './status.tsx'`, consistent with the rest of the test file.

The `'branch/group combined priority: error beats new'` test only calls `getMostCriticalStatusValue` — a pre-existing function that has its own test suite at the top of this file. It doesn't exercise any code added in this PR. Consider removing it or, if the priority of `error` over `new` under the updated `statusOrder` is specifically what needs verifying, add it to the existing `describe('getHighestStatus', ...)` block with a clear comment explaining why the ordering matters for the dual-slot feature.

general_comments.comment: `getChangeDetectionStatus` is a pure status utility (no JSX, no hooks, no component imports) but lives in `Tree.tsx`, a React component file. This forces `status.test.ts` to import from a component module and means the two closely related functions — `getChangeDetectionStatus` (Tree.tsx) and `getGroupDualStatus` (status.tsx) — are separated across files despite operating on the same domain. Moving `getChangeDetectionStatus` to `status.tsx` would co-locate all status logic, allow the test import to point at `./status.tsx`, and enable `getGroupDualStatus` to call it directly to remove the duplicated split logic.
